faq.q: Why does sugar cause holes in teeth?
faq.a: Germs in your mouth eat sugar and make acid. The acid slowly dissolves the hard enamel of your teeth, and over time this makes a hole.
A cavity is a hole in a tooth caused by decay. Small ones may not hurt, but deep ones can reach the nerve and cause toothache. A dentist can clean and fill it.

faq.q: How can I stop tooth decay?
faq.a: Brush for two minutes twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, keep sweet foods and drinks to mealtimes, drink water, and visit the dentist for check-ups.
asks: How do I keep my teeth healthy?

faq.a: Plaque is a sticky, colourless layer of germs that builds up on teeth. Brushing removes it before the germs can make lots of acid.
asks: What is the fuzzy stuff on my teeth?

faq.a: Fluoride makes tooth enamel harder and helps repair tiny early spots of acid damage, so holes are less likely to form.

facts: Bacteria in dental plaque turn sugars into acids that dissolve tooth enamel.
Dentists recommend brushing twice a day for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste.
